title: Irreversibility
hook: Most of the decisions you're agonizing over could be undone next week.
statement: Some decisions are easy to reverse and some aren't. Treat them differently.
explainer: If you can undo it, move fast and learn. If you can't, like a key hire or a big public promise, slow down and do the homework. Mixing them up kills momentum.
sop: Label the decision in front of you: reversible or permanent.
Score Irreversibility and Information Quality from 1 to 10.
If it's reversible, decide today and adjust later.
If it's permanent, gather more info before committing.
Double check it's truly permanent. Most things aren't.
equation_example: Irreversibility 3, Information Quality 8. (1 ÷ 3) × 8 = 2.7. Higher means go, you can undo it and you know enough. Lower means slow down and learn more before you commit.
question: Pick one decision you've been sitting on and write down whether it's actually reversible.
closing_statement: Undoable calls get speed. Permanent ones get patience.
